title: Tax on YouTube Income: A Guide for Indian Creators
description: Income earned by Indian content creators from YouTube is fully taxable in India. Earnings received in foreign currency, typically US Dollars, must be converte.

faq.q: Is YouTube income always considered business income?
faq.a: No, not always. While for most consistent creators it falls under "Profits and Gains from Business or Profession," if your earnings are very sporadic and not a result of sustained effort, it might be classified under "Income from Other Sources."

faq.q: Can I claim expenses for my home office?
faq.a: Yes, if you use a dedicated space in your home primarily for your YouTube work, you can claim a proportionate amount of expenses like rent, electricity, and internet as business expenses. You must be able to justify the proportion claimed.

faq.q: What exchange rate should I use for conversion?
faq.a: You can use the RBI reference rate prevailing on the date the income is credited to your bank account, or an average of the RBI reference rates for the financial year. Consistency in the method chosen is important.

faq.q: Do I need to pay advance tax?
faq.a: Yes, if your estimated tax liability for the financial year, after deducting TDS (if any), is ₹10,000 or more, you are required to pay advance tax in four instalments.

faq.q: What if I earn less than the basic exemption limit?
faq.a: If your total taxable income, including YouTube earnings, is below the basic exemption limit (currently ₹2.5 lakhs for individuals below 60 years), you may not have to pay tax. However, you might still need to file an ITR if your gross total income exceeds the basic exemption limit before claiming deductions.

faq.q: Is GST applicable on YouTube income?
faq.a: GST might be applicable if your aggregate turnover from all taxable supplies (including YouTube income) exceeds the threshold limits (currently ₹20 lakhs for services, ₹10 lakhs for special category states). You would need to register for GST and charge GST on services provided within India.

faq.q: What if I get income from multiple platforms (e.g., YouTube and Instagram)?
faq.a: Income from all such platforms is aggregated and treated as part of your "Profits and Gains from Business or Profession" if these are regular, profit-seeking activities. All related expenses can be claimed against the combined income.
